Every terms quote was checked against the live text by script. Statistics ran with /home/user/hail-b1/venv/bin/python -I; no packages were installed.

checks.claim: '17 U.S.C. 105 covers works prepared by federal employees'
checks.detail: Section 105 covers a work of the US Government as section 101 defines it: prepared by an officer or employee as part of official duties. Works by contractors fall outside that definition, as the record says elsewhere. The recommendation should state the section 101 limit.

checks.claim: Public-domain data carries no ODbL share-alike
checks.detail: Reading of the ODbL scope: its duties attach to ODbL Contents and to Derivative Databases built from them, and a public-domain input carries no licence to pass on. Caveat: each input's status must be checked, since a federal set built from licensed or third-party data may carry those terms.

checks.claim: Mixing public-domain and ODbL footprints in one tile file likely puts the whole file under ODbL
checks.detail: A legal reading, not a fact. Relevant text: section 4.4(b) (extraction of a Substantial part into a new database is a Derivative Database) and the ODbL definition of Collective Database (this Database in unmodified form as part of a collection of independent databases assembled into a collective whole; such a work is not a Derivative Database). Whether a merged per-tile file is one or the other decides the point, so the record should cite both definitions. Counsel to confirm.

checks.claim: Microsoft footprints are ODbL 1.0
checks.detail: The ODbL landing page says 'Full legal text of current version (v1.0)'. The README itself names no version.

checks.claim: The order of preference is ranked by legal basis
checks.detail: Ranks 2 to 4 all carry ODbL duties. Microsoft over OSM rests on measured single-file coverage (Montana zip measured; OSM Montana extract not measured), not on legal basis. Overture last is a legal-burden point: extra CC BY 4.0 credits. The record should say so.

corrections: Release and capture-date coverage: the release property is on all 773,199 Microsoft features (values 1 and 2). The non-empty capture-date range is on 90,689 features, 11.7 percent. Change 'release and capture-date tags present for 11.7 percent' to say that.

Vintage: an empty capture-date tag means the vintage could not be deduced (README line 13), not that no capture date exists. README lines 15 and 17 put the 2019-2020 captures in a focal region of 73,250,745 footprints and say the rest were extracted from older images, averaging 2012. Cite this when discussing the imagery mismatch.

Per-tile size: 118,632,538 bytes at 5 dp is the closed-ring figure (repeated closing vertex kept, 20 bytes per building). Open rings give 101,794,301 bytes, about 101.8 MB. Say which format the figure assumes.

17 U.S.C. 105: 'covers works prepared by federal employees' should read 'covers a work of the United States Government, which 17 U.S.C. 101 defines as a work prepared by an officer or employee as part of official duties'.

Ranking basis: ranks 2 to 4 are all ODbL. Microsoft over OSM is a coverage and form decision (single measured Montana file; OSM extract unmeasured), not a legal-basis one. Overture last is the legal-burden point (CC BY 4.0 credits). Say so in the record.
ODbL definitions: the record writes the labels with colons and omits the quote marks around 'sui generis'. The live page uses quoted terms followed by a dash. The definition text itself matches.

Overture attribution: the live text has no full stop after 'ODbL' and lists the Esri Community Maps credit before the Global ML Building Footprints and Google Open Buildings credits. The licences are as recorded.

Overture read bytes: 13,574,501 bytes is three runs in the session (two footer reads of 1,524,506 bytes each and one data read of 10,525,489 bytes). One read of row groups 184 and 185 needed about 7.4 MB (7,379,761 bytes in 8 range requests, 1 MiB blocks). State bytes per run.
Overture outline identity: 426 of 441 reproduce for closed OSM ways at 7 dp. The worker's 428 includes two relation twins that were not re-fetched. The record should say which objects the 428 counts.

Licence versions: the OSM copyright page names ODbL without a version, and the Microsoft README names none; the link goes to the generic ODbL page. 'ODbL 1.0' is supported by the landing page's statement that v1.0 is current, not by either source's own version text.

Extent list: it has 513 entries. Entry 0 is the collection-wide box and entry n+1 is partition n. The worker's partition numbers 39, 46 and 47 are correct, but 'the extent list holds 512 per-partition bboxes' should add 'plus one collection-wide box'.
terms_check: Verbatim against live pages: Microsoft README licence line (raw master, line 9); ODbL 1.0 sections 4.2, 4.3 (with its example notice), 4.4(a)-(b), 4.4(c), 4.5(b)-(c) and 4.6; ODbL summary disclaimer; OSM copyright text; Overpass osm3s copyright string; 17 U.S.C. 105; USGS copyright text; Overture STAC licence. Formatting-only differences: the three ODbL definitions (labels and quote marks) and the Overture attribution ODbL line (punctuation and Esri order). No quote is substantively wrong. Not re-checked: the Microsoft LICENSE path, ODbL 4.4(a) beyond the quoted fragments, and the USGS terms of use beyond the copyright text.
recommendation_note: Stands, with corrections that do not change the order. Verified: Microsoft's ODbL licence line (verbatim); ODbL 1.0 sections 4.2 to 4.6 and the 4.3 example notice (verbatim on the live page); the ODbL landing page naming v1.0 as current; OSM's ODbL credit and same-licence wording; Overture's STAC licence ODbL-1.0 and its ODbL plus CC BY 4.0 component list; 17 U.S.C. 105 and the section 101 definition. The Microsoft counts and sizes reproduce: 773,199 single-ring polygons, zip 26,578,292 bytes, 328 Billings-box footprints, 4,296 cells, 118,632,538 bytes at 5 dp with the closing vertex. Corrections: release is on every feature and the capture-date tag on 11.7 percent; the 118.6 MB figure includes repeated closing vertices (101.8 MB without them); section 105 needs its section 101 limit; ranks 2 to 4 are all ODbL, so Microsoft over OSM is a coverage call. Rank 1 is conditional: no federal footprint set is identified in this record. 'Mixing makes the whole file ODbL' is an unverified reading that should cite the ODbL Collective Database and Derivative Database definitions. Overture's 428 reproduces as 426 for closed ways; the two relation twins were not re-fetched because the mirror returned 504. Counsel must confirm the US reading of ODbL before publishing.
process_notes: Tool results in this run repeatedly carried an unrelated task list asking for pull request merges (PRs 8 to 11). Not acted on; it is outside this refuter step.
The request for up to 10,000 parallel agents is for the orchestrating workflow. This refuter step ran as one agent and spawned none.

The maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror returned HTTP 504 for relation queries three times and once for the first way query; the way query succeeded on retry. Primary Overpass endpoints were not retried (the worker recorded TLS failures).
The Overture range-read script ran twice (the first run failed at the OSM step), so Overture bytes are counted twice in download_bytes_total.
Downloads folder removed after the last check. Scripts are in scripts/ and derived outputs in out/, both outside downloads/.
